Duix.Heygem does cloning + NON-REAL-TIME batch synthesis.
Real-time interactive avatars need the paid duix.com platform.

So the architecture is segment-based:

splice in fresh clips as products, prices and answers change.

It degrades gracefully: if rendering falls behind, the loop keeps
playing valid older segments instead of going dead." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="400" x="40" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="one" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#3d7a2a;" value="1 · AVATAR + VOICE (one-off, ~1 day per presenter)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="400" x="40" y="360" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o1" parent="one" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="10-second video sample → Duix.Heygem clone" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="360" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o2" parent="one" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="voice sample → CosyVoice zero-shot clone" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="360" x="20" y="88" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o3" parent="one" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="⚠ WRITTEN CONSENT from the person cloned.

Text overlay + voice covers most of it, and the
operator console covers the rest." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="62" width="380" x="20" y="162" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="six" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="6 · ORDER

on-screen product card → existing storefront checkout
→ order-service, channel = LIVESTREAM

Register the channel in channel-service so pricing,
promotions and finance reporting work unchanged —
the same pattern as the ACP channel in N-03." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="350" x="1430" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="repos" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="Repos

duixcom/Duix.Heygem — 10s clone, offline,
 Docker Win/Ubuntu 22.04, ~100GB disk
 Lite build: 70GB → 13.5GB, audio-only
Caladog/HeyGem — one-click Windows, 8GB VRAM
CosyVoice — zero-shot + cross-lingual clone
QwenAudio/Fun-ASR — Apache-2.0, vLLM streaming
QwenLM/Qwen-Agent — Apache-2.0, MCP
op.jinritemai.com — ⚠ enterprise entity required" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="350" x="1430" y="330" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="meas" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="Measurement (I06 holdout)

GMV per stream hour · conversion per clip
watch time per segment · escalation rate

Holdout: human-run hours vs digital-human
hours on the SAME SKU set.

If digital-human hours underperform badly,
the honest output is "use it for off-peak
coverage only" — which is still valuable." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="210" width="350" x="1430" y="560" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="rule" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1" value="DESIGN RULE that makes this defensible: price and stock are NEVER inside the rendered video. They are overlays read live from the services.
Consent, labelling and the price-drift check are the three things a Chinese platform reviewer would actually test — so they are built in, not bolted on." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" div.div: Livestream GMV ¥7.2T (2025) → ¥9.08T forecast (2026). The 2025 shift was 店播 — MERCHANT-run streams, +45% YoY, 80,000+ merchants past ¥1M GMV. A KOL stream is a talent problem; a 24/7 store stream is a software problem.

div.div:
THE BLOCKER, stated up front
Duix.Heygem does cloning + NON-REAL-TIME batch synthesis.
Real-time interactive avatars need the paid duix.com platform.
So the architecture is segment-based:
pre-render a clip library → play it in a scheduled loop →
splice in fresh clips as products, prices and answers change.
It degrades gracefully: if rendering falls behind, the loop keeps
playing valid older segments instead of going dead.

6 · ORDER
on-screen product card → existing storefront checkout
→ order-service, channel = LIVESTREAM
Register the channel in channel-service so pricing,
promotions and finance reporting work unchanged —
the same pattern as the ACP channel in N-03.

div.div:
Repos
duixcom/Duix.Heygem — 10s clone, offline,
Docker Win/Ubuntu 22.04, ~100GB disk
Lite build: 70GB → 13.5GB, audio-only
Caladog/HeyGem — one-click Windows, 8GB VRAM
CosyVoice — zero-shot + cross-lingual clone
QwenAudio/Fun-ASR — Apache-2.0, vLLM streaming
QwenLM/Qwen-Agent — Apache-2.0, MCP
op.jinritemai.com — ⚠ enterprise entity required

div.div:
Measurement (I06 holdout)
GMV per stream hour · conversion per clip
watch time per segment · escalation rate
Holdout: human-run hours vs digital-human
hours on the SAME SKU set.
If digital-human hours underperform badly,
the honest output is "use it for off-peak
coverage only" — which is still valuable.

div.div:
DESIGN RULE that makes this defensible: price and stock are NEVER inside the rendered video. They are overlays read live from the services.
Consent, labelling and the price-drift check are the three things a Chinese platform reviewer would actually test — so they are built in, not bolted on.
